limitations: Short sample: one 64-session window (SPY -4.6 pp); no rebound or crash regime was observed.
Annualised differentials from 63 daily returns are very noisy; read total-window differences and their intervals.

Population (deviation D5): 16 outage-reconstructed plans (13 receipted replays, 3 synthetic-board reconstructions) are excluded because their earliest auditable availability is after their nominal publication session; the correction was made after outcomes were seen, follows a rule that predates the evaluation, and lowers the headline.

X6 is an exposure-weight arithmetic reference, not a selection-matched comparator: it matches only risky weight, so K2 nearly repeats K1. A comparator matched on eligible cohort, concentration, sector/factor exposure, timing and costs requires a new pre-declared protocol; X6 is not replaced retrospectively.

Undated conversions: 78 era plans are terminal-state 'converted' with no dated fill in the snapshot; the C6 rule enters them at publication because the header's literal text admits it. Excluding every one of them moves the book to -5.7% total, -1.1 pp versus SPY (CI [-12.1, +9.5] pp, still spans zero). Found by the 2026-11-11 independent audit; the sensitivity is not part of the frozen protocol.

Missing held marks: 2 held positions own assets whose close series stops inside the window (delistings); the primary book zero-fills them (held flat), which flatters the book relative to an unknown true price. A total-loss stress (-4.4% total, +0.2 pp versus SPY, CI [-11.6, +11.9] pp) bounds the damage; the affected positions are listed in coverage.held_path_gap_positions.

Coverage basis: the 95%+ priced-share gate is measured on ENTRY marks only. It says nothing about marks after entry — the gapped held positions above are priced at entry and then run flat, so the gate passes while held-path completeness is a separate, disclosed quantity.

Cost conventions (header-decided, stated plainly): costs are per side on traded notional at trade close, including the terminal trade (corrected 2026-11-11); C1 is 100% SPY held through the window with no terminal sale; the uninvested weight earns BIL without fee; X6 is arithmetic and cost-free by definition; annualisation is arithmetic (mean daily differential x 252) throughout.

Yardstick: the event study's stock-minus-sector-ETF leg grades picks against a cap-weighted fund. The equal-weight member benchmark (event_study.member_benchmark, added 2026-11-11) shows an average same-sector member trailing that fund by -0.6 pp at 21 sessions and -2.1 pp at 42; that share of the published leg is the yardstick, not member choice.

Off-index names: 46 published plans (6% of them) name stocks outside the point-in-time S&P 1500 at the signal date and carried -0.6 pp of the 21-session mean gap; the membership file records no change after 2026-06-02, so late-window non-membership is uncertain in both directions (see sensitivity.off_index_picks.membership_file_limits).

the 2026-08-19 one-day close move of +177% (62.96 -> 174.38; raw and adjusted closes agree; volume 199,252,300) was, at publication, present only in the single price cache used by this runner. Two post-publication second-source checks (independent audit RUN-D 2026-11-11) now authenticate it: a ChartExchange end-of-day sweep reproduces the 62.96 -> 174.38 closes, and a Yahoo live-chart API pull matches all 64 window sessions for MRNA. Both are audit evidence gathered after outcomes were seen, labelled as such, and change no frozen number; the v1 caveat is retained here superseded.; it affects any population that admits the replayed plans.
S&P 1500 point-in-time membership has no recorded change after 2026-06-02; 35 point-in-time members had no price file and were excluded.
Sector labels are current-basis GICS, not the classification in force at each date.

Prophet plans are read from the 2026-11-09 plan snapshot, not each plan's as-published bytes; entries use the publication clock and close-only fills, so results differ from the plan record's own same-bar outcomes.

Model book: equal weight across open positions (per position, not per distinct ticker; no same-ticker overlaps occur in this sample, so the two coincide here). It is not user holdings, a portfolio recommendation or sizing advice.
The event-study date-cluster intervals treat publication dates as independent although nearby dates share overlapping market paths, so those intervals are likely too narrow.
Issuer-excluded peer counts are unavailable: identity is the listing ticker only.
The eight catalog sleeves cannot be evaluated: plans carry no sleeve link. admission_class strata are reported instead.

headline: Release level: descriptive only (L0). The predeclared global minimum for any accepted historical claim requires all of: 252 sessions (this window has 64), an 8% SPY drawdown (deepest here is -5.9%) and 150 resolved positions (this window has 308 — the only gate that passes). Two of three fail, so every job stays L0.
Market over the window: SPY -4.6% total return, deepest drawdown -5.9%.

Population: live-published plans only. 16 outage-reconstructed plans that no user could see on their nominal publication dates are excluded from every headline number (deviation D5); the superseded as-run numbers are retained under sensitivity.superseded_as_run.

Corrected 2026-11-11 after a two-run independent audit: final-close trade costs are now charged and price bytes are verified against the data pin (v1 C6 total was -3.1%). Superseded figures sit beside the corrected ones; the verdict — L0, not distinguishable from passive — is unchanged.

Incumbent Prophet book (as built, 498 positions): -3.2% net, +1.4 pp versus SPY, 95% CI [-10.5, +13.2] pp. The interval includes zero: this is not evidence of outperformance, and the sample is far too short.
Beta capture: beta 0.79 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.08), mean invested weight 98%; upside capture 0.93, downside capture 0.88.

Without its largest single contributor (AMR) the book is +0.7 pp versus SPY (CI [-10.7, +11.9] pp); without the three largest (AMR, CRCL, TEM) it is -0.4 pp — the sign of the whole result rests on three names.

Live-published plans held for a fixed 21 sessions without Prophet's exits differed from SPY by -3.0 pp on average (date-cluster CI [-5.1, -0.9] pp); most of that gap was the stock versus its own sector ETF, not the sector choice.

That stock-versus-sector number has two floors under it. An average point-in-time member of the same sector trailed its own cap-weighted fund by -0.6 pp at 21 sessions — that floor is the yardstick, not member choice. The picks sat a further -2.4 pp below that average member (CI [-3.5, -1.3] pp); a random-member placebo over the same dates and sectors lands inside -1.6 pp to +0.5 pp. The independent diagnosis attributes more of the remainder to the characteristics of what was picked (short-term bounce, medium-term laggards, off-index speculative names); what is left does not survive its multiplicity correction. No claim of negative member selection, and no claim of its absence.

Sector rotation alone, sector-neutral member selection alone and their combination did not beat SPY on this window (K3 -4.0 pp/yr, K4 -4.3 pp/yr, K5 -7.6 pp/yr annualised; none significant after Holm). Insignificant results mean value is not shown, not that there is none.

The exposure-matched reference (X6) is an exposure-weight arithmetic reference only: it matches risky weight alone, and because the book is essentially fully invested, K2 nearly repeats the SPY comparison (K1) and cannot identify member-selection value.
Prophet plans inside leading sectors did better than plans outside them in this window (K7 +11.7 pp/yr annualised, Holm p 1.00); this is not significant.
Nothing here shows that sector context or member selection adds value beyond market participation.
